title: Deterministic parallel perfect matching in general graphs
decision_reason: Explicit sourced formulation, independent corroboration, current resolution searches, twelve-source scope audit, duplicate checks, separated A67 self-review and final technical validation passed. One pending family; no permanent ID.

problem_fingerprint.model_or_objects: Every finite labelled simple undirected graph G=([n],E), n>=2, encoded by its binomial(n,2) adjacency bits.
problem_fingerprint.solution: A subset M of E in which every vertex has exactly one incident edge; output a perfect matching if one exists, otherwise report that none exists.
problem_fingerprint.requested_conclusion: A deterministic logspace-uniform Boolean circuit family, polynomial size and polylogarithmic depth, solving the search problem on every input graph.
problem_fingerprint.uniformity: One deterministic machine, given 1^n, writes the circuit description with O(log n) work space. Gates are AND/OR of fan-in two, NOT, and constants; outputs encode a success bit and a matching's edge-incidence vector.
problem_fingerprint.quantifiers: Universal fixed constants K,c,k>0 bound circuit size by K*n^c and depth by K*(log_2(n+2))^k. No randomness, advice, graph-class restriction, promise that a matching exists, approximate answer or unbounded-bit arithmetic.
problem_fingerprint.scope: Constructing an unweighted perfect matching. Merely deciding existence is not declared equivalent. The known search reduction uses a polynomially bounded weighted decision oracle.
problem_fingerprint.family_policy: One general-graph parallel-matching entry; bipartite and planar classes, weighted companions and isolation-based approaches are not separately counted or claimed equivalent.

statement_sources.locator: Section 1, pp.2–3, and Section 1.4, p.9; exact general-graph decision/search questions.
Definition 7.1, p.81, and Open question 7, p.123; logspace-uniform NC convention.
Introduction and Theorem 1, pp.54:1–54:2; independent search question and weighted-oracle limitation.

nearest_existing_entries.difference: General rational arithmetic-circuit identity testing in sequential polynomial time; the present graph problem is already in sequential polynomial time and asks for polylogarithmic parallel depth.
Existence of short paths in polytope graphs, not a matching construction algorithm; a matching-polytope reference does not make the assertions equivalent.
One spanning tree with simultaneous cut bounds; its perfect-matching comparison concerns thinness, not parallel complexity.
Existence of edge-specific list colourings with no extra colours, without a complexity bound; not construction of a single vertex-covering matching.

resolution_comparisons.result_scope: Tutte ordinary rank detects integral matching; noncommutative rank detects fractional matching.
resolution_comparisons.comparison_with_target: The triangle ranks are 2 and 3. CGGRT26 Theorem 1.5 cannot simply substitute noncommutative rank for ordinary rank.

normalization_checks: Vertex count n and adjacency input length binomial(n,2) differ polynomially; the circuit and uniformity classes agree.
Bounded-fan-in Boolean gates; no advice, random bits, unbounded-bit unit-time arithmetic, graph-class restriction or existence promise.
Success bit handles nonexistence, including odd n; output is an actual perfect matching, not size or a fractional vector.
Unweighted search-to-decision equivalence is not assumed; the NC reduction uses weighted threshold decision.
Quasipolynomial work, catalytic workspace and polynomial time do not meet the requested circuit bounds.
LM26 accuracy is fixed; input-dependent accuracy changes its complexity bound.
One general-graph family counted; restricted graph classes, weighting and isolation are context.
Application concerns asymptotic pairwise scheduling capability, not empirical hardware or distributed-network guarantees.
